core_obligations: Set up the situation of the derived functor theory with D = K(O_Y), D' = D(O_X), F induced by f^* and S the quasi-isomorphisms, so that the definition of a left derived functor applies (proof lines 6338-6350).

Show that the left derived functor is everywhere defined by taking P to be the K-flat complexes: condition (1) is the existence of K-flat resolutions, and condition (2) reduces to the claim below (proof lines 6352-6356).

Verify condition (2): for a quasi-isomorphism K_1 to K_2 between K-flat complexes of O_Y-modules, rewrite the induced map as a map of tensor products over f^{-1}O_Y; exactness of f^{-1} makes it a quasi-isomorphism of K-flat complexes of f^{-1}O_Y-modules, so tensoring over f^{-1}O_Y does not destroy the quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 6357-6376).
Conclude that LF exists, is the derived pullback, and is computed on K-flat complexes by F itself (proof lines 6378-6390).
proof_roadmap: Invoke the derived functor framework (proof lines 6338-6350).
Choose the K-flat complexes as the resolving class (proof lines 6352-6356).
Prove that pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes (proof lines 6357-6376).
Read off the existence and the computation rule (proof lines 6378-6390).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the construction of the derived pullback given just before it is independent of choices and defines an exact functor of triangulated categories Lf^*: D(O_Y) to D(O_X) (statement lines 6329-6334). The proof is an application of the general existence machinery for derived functors: with D = K(O_Y), D' = D(O_X), F the exact functor induced by f^* and S the quasi-isomorphisms, the author verifies the hypotheses that make the left derived functor everywhere defined, taking P to be the class of K-flat complexes (proof lines 6336-6350). The only step needing an argument is condition (2): for a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes of O_Y-modules, the induced map on pullbacks is a quasi-isomorphism, which is proved by rewriting the pullback as a tensor product over f^{-1}O_Y, using exactness of f^{-1} and the fact that both complexes stay K-flat after applying f^{-1} (proof lines 6352-6376). The claim is H2: the framework is cited wholesale, but the verification of the K-flat hypothesis is a real computation and is where the choice of P is justified.
